entries.title: Structural topology closure failed

examples: A reachable instance refers to a missing structural specialization.
repairs: Correct the first topology-closure diagnostic and rerun acc.py.

A definition cannot be assigned to exactly one AC package unit.
examples: Two source files differ only by a portable-path case fold and would publish the same AC unit.
repairs: Correct the selected root, source provenance, or readable package path and regenerate the AC package.

repairs: Inspect the accompanying stage and source diagnostic, then correct the first reported failure.

entries.title: Defensive guard for child static-argument rendering
entries.rule: This code is a defensive guard, not a reachable contract: every supported lowering entry point supplies the static-argument renderer for a child instance, so a child with static arguments cannot reach this branch through supported input.
causes: A direct caller of lower_queue_program supplied child instances with static arguments but no static-argument renderer.
examples: ac.instance @child_0 of @child(...) static #ac.static_arguments<[]>
repairs: Lower the module body through lower_queue_source or lower_module_source, which supply the static-argument renderer.

entries.title: Local rule in a segmented module body has unsupported results
entries.rule: A rule-backed module body that places child instances lowers a stateless single-result local rule to one transform and a stateless multi-result local rule to one multi-output firing block. A local rule that owns Table or Var state still has no representation there, so it must produce exactly one Queue.
causes: A segmented rule-backed module body calls a stateful local rule with more than one result, or a local rule with no result.
examples: thread0, thread1 = route(count, request)
repairs: Make the multi-result rule stateless, split it into single-result stateless rules, or move the stateful child calls into their own module.

entries.title: Segmented module body cannot resolve a Queue mapping
entries.rule: Every Queue consumed inside a segmented module body has a producer mapping, so the frontend never emits an unresolved Queue reference.
causes: A fanout broadcast crosses a child instance boundary in a shape the segment renderer cannot thread.
examples: r0 = mk(request); child = state_bank(other); r1 = dup(r0); r2 = dup(r0)
repairs: Reorder the body so a fanout's consumers share one segment, or route the shared value through an explicit child module.
